e-8729.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a One-Dimensional Subspace
e-8729.problem:
Let $V = \Bbb R_1[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
\langle p(t),q(t) \rangle = p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $p(t)=-5t-3$ onto the subspace spanned by the polynomial $q(t) =t-1.$
e-8729.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{ q(t) \}$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{q(t)}\,p(t) 
= \dfrac{\langle{p(t),q(t)}\rangle}{\langle{q(t),q(t)}\rangle}\,q(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(-5t-3){|}_{0}\cdot (t-1){|}_{0}+(-5t-3){|}_{1}\cdot (t-1){|}_{1} \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)+(-8)\cdot 0 \\  & =3+0 \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),q(t)⟩ & =q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1) \\  & =(t-1){|}_{0}\cdot (t-1){|}_{0}+(t-1){|}_{1}\cdot (t-1){|}_{1} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0 \\  & =1+0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{3}{1}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =3(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

e-8730.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
e-8730.problem:
Let $V = \mathcal{C}[-1,1],$ the vector space of continuous functions over $[-1,1]$, and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
\langle x(t),y(t) \rangle =\int_{-1}^{1} x(t) y(t) \, \text{d}t.
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V\mathbin{:}$

$$
f_1(t)=1,\quad f_2(t)=\sin \pi t, \quad g(t)=6t^2
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}\{f_1(t), f_2(t)\}$ given that $f_1(t) \perp f_2(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{f_1(t)\}$ equals $2.$
e-8730.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{f_1(t),f_2(t)\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,g(t) 
= \textrm{proj}_{f_1(t)}\,g(t) + \textrm{proj}_{f_2(t)}\,g(t).
$$

We are given that $\textrm{proj}_{f_1(t)}\,g(t) = 2,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{f_2(t)\}.$ This can be computed as

$$
\textrm{proj}_{f_2(t)}\,g(t) 
= \dfrac{\langle{g(t),f_2(t)}\rangle}{\langle{f_2(t),f_2(t)}\rangle}\,f_2(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}g(t){f}_{2}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}6{t}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}6{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sin (\pi t)$ is an odd function, while $6t^2$ is even. Hence, their product $6 t^2 \sin (\pi t)$ must be an odd function. Now, since we have an integral over the interval $[-1,1],$ which is symmetric about the origin, we can conclude that

$$
\int_{-1}^{1}   6t^2 \sin (\pi t) \, \text{d}t = 0.
$$

  

Therefore,

$$
\textrm{proj}_{f_2(t)}\,g(t) = \dfrac{0}{\langle{f_2(t),f_2(t)}\rangle} \cdot  \sin \pi t = 0.
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t) \\  & =2+0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

The orthogonal projection of p(t) onto Span{q(t)} is given by

projq(t)p(t)=⟨p(t),q(t)⟩⟨q(t),q(t)⟩q(t).

In our case, we have

⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(−1)q(−1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)=(t2+3t−2)|t=−1⋅(2t−2)|t=−1+(t2+3t−2)|t=0⋅(2t−2)|t=0+(t2+3t−2)|t=1⋅(2t−2)|t=1=(−4)⋅(−4)+(−2)⋅(−2)+2⋅0=16+4=20,

and

⟨q(t),q(t)⟩=q(−1)q(−1)+q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1)=(2t−2)|t=−1⋅(2t−2)|t=−1+(2t−2)|t=0⋅(2t−2)|t=0+(2t−2)|t=1⋅(2t−2)|t=1=(−4)⋅(−4)+(−2)⋅(−2)+0⋅0=16+4+0=20.

Therefore, the projection is

projq(t)p(t)=⟨p(t),q(t)⟩⟨q(t),q(t)⟩q(t)=2020⋅(2t−2)=2t−2.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $p(t)=-3t-2$ onto the subspace spanned by the polynomial $q(t)=t.$
after.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)=\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(-3t-2){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(-3t-2){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =(-2)\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1 \\  & =0-5 \\  & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),q(t)⟩ & =q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1) \\  & =(t){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(t){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1 \\  & =0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{-5}{1}\cdot t \\  & =-5t.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $p(t)=-3t-2$ onto the subspace spanned by the polynomial $q(t)=t.$
content.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)=\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(-3t-2){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(-3t-2){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =(-2)\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1 \\  & =0-5 \\  & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),q(t)⟩ & =q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1) \\  & =(t){|}_{0}\cdot (t){|}_{0}+(t){|}_{1}\cdot (t){|}_{1} \\  & =0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1 \\  & =0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{-5}{1}\cdot t \\  & =-5t.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)=-5t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{2}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t)=\frac{⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}{⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}\,{p}_{2}(t).

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & =q(0){p}_{2}(0)+q(1){p}_{2}(1) \\  & =(-t-4){|}_{0}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{0}+(-t-4){|}_{1}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{1} \\  & =(-4)\cdot 2+(-5)\cdot 0 \\  & =-8,\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Question 8

Let V=R2[t], the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most 2, and let the inner product on V be defined as ⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(−1)q(−1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).

Now consider the following elements of V:

p1(t)=t2+t,p2(t)=t2−t,q(t)=7t−3

Find the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto S=Span{p1(t),p2(t)} given that p1(t)⊥p2(t) with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto Span{p1(t)} equals 2t2+2t.

a
7t2−3t
b
t2−7
c
t2+7t
d
3t2−7t
e
−3t2+7t

decision.explanation: Since p₁ and p₂ are orthogonal, their projections add. At -1,0,1, p₂ has values 2,0,0, so ⟨q,p₂⟩=(-10)(2)=-20 and ⟨p₂,p₂⟩=4. Thus the projection onto p₂ is -5(t²-t). Adding the given 2t²+2t yields -3t²+7t.
